name: Animal cell
short_description: The umbrella subject closing the organelles set: the generic textbook animal cell — an irregularly rounded bag of cytoplasm bounded only by its plasma membrane, shown in cutaway with the set's parts assembled in place: nucleus with nucleolus and pores, rough ER continuous with the nuclear envelope, smooth ER, a separate Golgi stack with budding vesicles, several cristae-filled mitochondria, lysosomes, free ribosomes, a centriole pair and cytoskeleton filaments.

textbook.1: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; style and palette on-house and no baked text, but the nuclear layering is inverted: the lumpy dusty-purple heterochromatin mass is painted OUTSIDE the blue double envelope ring, wrapping it like a rind, instead of hugging the envelope's inner face. Rough ER also floats free of the nucleus. Fix-prompt: heterochromatin clumps pressed against the INNER face of the envelope, envelope the outermost line of the nucleus, rough ER cisternae growing out of the outer envelope line)
textbook.2: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; the centrioles came out as exactly two barrels in a T — correct — but the heterochromatin rind is again outside the blue envelope ring, and the rough ER stack ends blind next to the nucleus rather than flowing out of it. Same inverted-nucleus fix-prompt as attempt 1, stated more positively)
textbook.3: pass-with-compromises (gemini-2.5-flash-image; ACCEPTED as the textbook final and the primary labelled figure. Verified on magnified crops of all four quadrants: no letters, numbers or labels anywhere — the amber pore motifs on the envelope carry tiny tick-dashes that stay abstract at 3x zoom. Irregular lumpy outline with a single thin teal membrane line; heterochromatin now correctly INSIDE the envelope, hugging its inner face around lavender euchromatin and one terracotta nucleolus with no boundary line; rough ER as connected dotted grey-blue cisternae reaching the envelope on the left; smooth dot-free tubules elsewhere; ONE separate sage-green Golgi stack of 6 cisternae with vesicle dots around its rims; I count 5 bean mitochondria, each double-outlined with wavy dusty-rose cristae ribbons; 5-6 speckled single-membrane mauve lysosomes; free-ribosome dot scatter; fine thread strokes for cytoskeleton. MEASURED COMPROMISES, all recorded: (a) the centriole cluster shows FOUR amber barrels in two parallel pairs, not the two-barrel right-angle pair the brief asked for — biologically readable as a duplicated centrosome (two centriole pairs, as in G2), so the SVG label says 'Centrioles' rather than 'Centriole pair'; (b) the nuclear envelope reads as one thick dark-blue band with light edge lines rather than two cleanly separate parallel lines with a pale gap; (c) two long pale sage-green arcs sweep through the cytoplasm parallel to the membrane — best read as cortical cytoskeleton filaments, though they are wider than the other thread strokes)
textbook.4: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; the explicit exactly-two-barrels instruction produced two barrels but drifted the rest: the two barrels sit far apart on opposite sides of the nucleus instead of touching as a pair, the rough ER became thick torn-ended sausage tubes disconnected from the envelope, a stray green halo band circles the nucleus, and the two large salmon organelles read as folded ribbon masses without the mitochondrion's smooth double-membrane capsule. Organelle identity is muddier than attempt 3 throughout)
textbook.5: fail (gemini-3-pro-image, escalation after two genuine flash failures; the science and house style are the best of the run BUT the render is fully lettered: printed callouts with leader lines everywhere - 'plasma membrane', 'lysosome', 'rough endoplasmic reticulum', even the raw hex codes #7B4B8A / #C9A6D6 / #D9622B from the prompt's colour legend baked into the image. The classic failure mode for this most label-contaminated of all textbook subjects, on the model tier that is best at text. Unusable; labels must be SVG layers)

sem.1: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; convincing false-colour SEM material, but the composition is a near-perfect fourfold mandala: four radial spikes/cracks at 12-3-6-9 o'clock, the ER as concentric onion rings all the way around the nucleus, and the mitochondria cristae drawn as crossed X-lattice struts rather than parallel shelves. Real fractured cells are asymmetric. Fix-prompt: asymmetric diagonal fracture, ER swept to one flank, cristae as parallel wavy shelves)
sem.2: partial (gemini-2.5-flash-image; better - fracture texture, beaded rough-ER band, nucleus with nucleolus dome, no text - but still radially symmetric like a sliced onion, and every mitochondrion's cristae are again a criss-cross diagonal lattice instead of roughly parallel shelves; the grey cytoskeleton filaments read as cracks crossing the whole plate. Second genuine quality failure on flash for this style -> escalate)
sem.3: pass (gemini-3-pro-image, escalation after two flash failures; ACCEPTED as the sem final. Verified on magnified crops of all four quadrants: no letters, numbers or scale bars anywhere. A single irregularly-domed cell on a textured substrate, fractured open from one side at a diagonal - genuinely asymmetric this time. Teal dimpled outer surface; warm tan granular fracture cytoplasm; dusty-violet nucleus dome with a wedge broken out showing coarse granular chromatin and one smoother deeper-violet nucleolus lobe; layered blue-grey ER lamellae swept around/behind the nucleus with fine ribosome beading clearly visible on their faces; I count 5 coral mitochondria broken in cross-section, and in each the cristae now read as roughly PARALLEL wavy shelves attached to a double-layered rim (checked at 2x zoom on three of them); several smooth mauve lysosome globes; thin filament strands bridging the fracture. Honest note: a few filaments attach to mitochondria like tethers, reading more like guy-wires than cytoskeleton, and the nuclear envelope's two membrane surfaces are only hinted at along the torn rim - both acceptable at SEM-plate realism)

3d.1: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; natural tints and good Golgi/mitochondria, but the nuclear pores are glowing pale blobs smeared around the envelope, a large maroon convoluted mass at bottom centre reads as a second unexplained Golgi/ER hybrid organelle, and glassy pin-with-ball artifacts stick out of the Golgi region like cocktail sticks. Fix-prompt: pores as small crisp amber portholes, one Golgi only, no glassy pins)
3d.2: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; the nucleus is split open like a clamshell into two separate hemispheres with the heterochromatin clusters sitting on the OUTSIDE of both shells, and the cytoskeleton is drawn as thick white coral branches. Two genuine quality failures on flash -> escalate)
3d.3: pass (gemini-3-pro-image, escalation after two flash failures; ACCEPTED as the 3d final and labelled. Verified on magnified crops of all four quadrants plus a centriole close-up: no letters or numbers anywhere. Irregular translucent bag with one thin glossy teal membrane and a wedge cutaway; nucleus with TWO distinct concentric blue envelope shells, a visible gap, and crisp small amber porthole pores; dusty-purple heterochromatin clumps INSIDE against the rim, lavender fibres central, one smooth terracotta nucleolus with no shell; grey rough-ER sheets flowing out of the outer envelope shell, densely studded with dark ribosome beads; smooth unbeaded tubules continuing outward at right; ONE separate sage-green Golgi stack (6 sacs) with budding rim vesicles; centriole close-up shows EXACTLY TWO barrels, each a bundle of microtubule rods, oriented roughly perpendicular; mauve lysosomes with granular interiors (two drawn as cut-open cups, consistent with the cutaway convention); free-ribosome specks throughout; fine pale filaments to the membrane. MEASURED: 7 mitochondria with wavy dusty-rose cristae - more than the prompt's three-to-five, harmless since several stand for hundreds)

watercolor.1: partial (gemini-2.5-flash-image; full-bleed paper and correct nucleus, ER attached to the envelope - but the centrioles appear as FOUR barrels in two separate locations (a duplicated centrosome split across the cell) and each mitochondrion's cristae are a single thin squiggle rather than wide ribbons)
watercolor.2: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; the rough ER became a field of separate dotted rice-grain sacs that read as a colony of bacteria rather than one connected membrane system, the heterochromatin scalloped ring again bulges outside the envelope, three centriole barrels, and a heavy muddy brown halo. Fix-prompt: ER as one connected folded ribbon system out of the nucleus's outer line)
watercolor.3: partial (gemini-2.5-flash-image; the best flash watercolor - full-bleed paper, chromatin inside the envelope, amber pores, separate Golgi, four mitochondria with proper wide rose ribbons, no text - but the centriole cluster counts FIVE parallel barrels (verified on a 4x crop), and the rough-ER ribbons fray toward the plasma membrane instead of growing out of the nuclear envelope. Third flash attempt still failing the same countable feature -> escalate)
watercolor.4: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; the exactly-two-barrels fix worked - two near-parallel barrels - but the rough ER mutated into four closed sausage sacs with dotted rims and pink squiggle interiors, indistinguishable from extra mitochondria, and the cell sits on a bulging pale double-lobe that reads as a second body behind it. Fourth flash attempt; escalated to pro for the final try)
watercolor.5: pass-with-compromises (gemini-3-pro-image, escalation after repeated flash failures on the centriole count; ACCEPTED as the watercolor final, labelled black-on-paper. Attempt number 5 because attempt 4 was the last flash try. Verified on magnified crops of all four quadrants plus a centriole close-up: no letters or numbers anywhere; warm aged paper fills the frame corner-to-corner with a soft grey wash halo painted directly on the paper. Centriole close-up shows EXACTLY TWO ribbed barrels touching at a right angle - the countable feature finally correct. Nucleus with blue double-arc envelope segments, amber pore dots, purple chromatin clouds inside, one soft terracotta nucleolus blot without outline; rough ER as one connected system of long dotted grey-blue ribbon folds around the nucleus; smooth branching dot-free tubules at upper left; I count 5 mitochondria, each with parallel wavy dusty-rose cristae ribbons; 6 speckled mauve lysosome blots; ribosome dot scatter; fine ink cytoskeleton threads. MEASURED COMPROMISES: (a) TWO sage-green Golgi stacks (upper right and lower left) instead of the brief's single stack - biologically defensible (real cells hold many stacks; the sci text says so) and the label anchors the upper one; (b) the cutaway is a pie-slice wedge removed from the cell revealing plain tan paper underneath, a stylised naturalist convention rather than a sectioned interior; (c) the rough-ER ribbons ring the nucleus concentrically and their contact with the envelope's outer line is suggested rather than explicit)

reference: pass (Wikimedia Commons "Clara cell lung - TEM.jpg", Public domain, Louisa Howard, Rippel Electron Microscope Facility, Dartmouth College, JEOL 100CX TEM - the same trusted PD REMF source as this set's Golgi and nucleus plates. Viewed directly: a genuine TEM thin section through a mammalian bronchiolar (Club) cell showing the assembled interior this subject teaches - nucleus at lower right with textbook heterochromatin mottling and one prominent round dense nucleolus, sweeping stacked ER lamellae filling the upper cytoplasm, several dark mitochondria at lower left (cristae faintly resolvable in the largest), and the soft boundary against a neighbouring cell at upper right. Honest caveats: a PARTIAL cell, not a full-profile cell with its whole membrane in frame - at this magnification a whole 20 um cell and readable organelles cannot share one plate; no Golgi, lysosome or centriole is resolvable in this particular section; membranes' double lines are below the plate's resolution. Cleaning was a plain deterministic crop, no image-editing model: the baked-in footer band (500 nm scale bar, '06LungTEM', '1/7/0 REMF', bottom ~25 px of the 640x480 original) was cropped off, then a 455x455 square (x 185..640) keeping nucleus + nucleolus + ER + mitochondria, then a LANCZOS upscale of 2.37x to 1080x1080 - stated explicitly. Raw download kept beside it for provenance)
decision: use gen-03 (gemini-2.5-flash-image) as final and primary labelled figure. Attempts 1-2 inverted the nucleus (heterochromatin outside the envelope); attempt 3 fixed it and passed the magnified-crop text check. Accepted compromise: the centriole cluster shows four barrels (two duplicated pairs) instead of two, so the label reads 'Centrioles' not 'Centriole pair'; attempt 4 (flash, two-barrel fix) degraded organelle identity and attempt 5 (pro) baked full printed labels including hex codes into the plate - the subject's known dominant failure - so the clean attempt 3 wins at 5/5 attempts used

use gen-03 (gemini-3-pro-image) as final; flash produced a fourfold mandala with X-lattice cristae twice, pro delivered an asymmetric fracture with parallel-shelf cristae, beaded ER and no text on the first pro try. Not labelled (SEM is the surface/cutaway comparison plate, per the set's convention)

use gen-03 (gemini-3-pro-image) as final; labelled figure built. Flash failed twice (smeared glowing pores + phantom maroon organelle + glass-pin artifacts; then a clamshell nucleus with chromatin outside). Pro landed every structure on its first try; exactly two perpendicular centriole barrels confirmed on a close-up crop; 7 mitochondria counted (brief said several)

use gen-05 (gemini-3-pro-image) as final, labelled black-on-paper. Flash tried four times and never got the centriole count and the connected-ER reading right in the same image (4, 3, 5, then 2 barrels but ER as mito-lookalike sacs); pro fixed the pair and the connected dotted ER in one pass. Accepted compromises: a second Golgi stack (biologically defensible), and the cutaway wedge exposes plain paper rather than sectioned cytosol
